Definition: probably from ῥόδον (a rose); Rhodus, an island of the Mediterranean:--Rhodes.
BiblicalUsage: After they had parted from the elders of Ephesus, they came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, on the way to Jerusalem. The ship had sailed a straight course from Coos, and Rhodes was the next harbour on the way to Jerusalem.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the islands of Paul's voyage are named because the journey was real, and every harbour mattered.
